proposals.before: The emperor immediately reassigned Zhang to Guangzhou as chief secretary and rewarded Xunzhi with a hundred bolts of silk.
proposals.after: The emperor immediately reassigned Zhang as chief clerk of Guang Prefecture and rewarded Xunzhi with a hundred bolts of silk.
proposals.reason: 光州 is Guang Prefecture, not Guangzhou (廣州); 長史 is the prefectural chief-clerk office.

proposals.before: The emperor at once transferred Zhang to long-term assignment in Guangzhou and gave Xunzhi a hundred bolts of silk.
proposals.after: The emperor at once transferred Zhang to be Chief Clerk of Guang Prefecture and gave Xunzhi a hundred bolts of silk.
proposals.reason: 長史 is an office title, not a long-term assignment; 光州 is Guang Prefecture, not Guangzhou.

proposals.before: Yixing said: "Lately treacherous ministers have repeatedly meddled in power; I beg Your Majesty not to hold the great hilt reversed and hand the blade to others."
proposals.after: Yixing said: "Lately treacherous ministers have repeatedly meddled in power; I beg Your Majesty not to hold the great sword reversed and hand the pommel to others."
proposals.reason: 倒持大阿，以鐏授人 means holding the sword by the blade and offering the pommel (鐏); the literal swaps hilt and blade.

proposals.before: Fengji wished to bring in Niu Sengru and, fearing that Shen and others in close attendance at court would obstruct the plan, appointed Deyu military commissioner of Zhexi.
proposals.after: Fengji wished to bring in Niu Sengru and, fearing that Shen and others in close attendance at court would obstruct the plan, appointed Deyu observation commissioner of Zhexi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 觀察使 is observation commissioner, not military commissioner (節度使); the idiomatic field already has the correct office.

proposals.before: Shen and Yu indeed would not yield to each other; they cited censorate precedents back and forth in mutual accusation until slander filled the air; for this both were removed, and Shen was made military commissioner of Jiangxi.
proposals.after: Shen and Yu indeed would not yield to each other; they cited censorate precedents back and forth in mutual accusation until slander filled the air; for this both were removed, and Shen was made observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 江西觀察使 is observation commissioner; literal incorrectly says military commissioner.

proposals.before: When Zhen became chief minister, Li Fengji engineered an accusation in the Fang affair and had him dismissed;
proposals.after: When Zhen became chief minister, Li Fengji engineered an accusation in the Yu Fang affair and had him dismissed;
proposals.reason: Chinese 於方事 names the Yu Fang (於方) case; English 'Fang affair' obscures the personal name established in the source.

proposals.before: In the Taihe era, when Li Deyu held power, Shen was promoted to military commissioner of Zhedong.
proposals.after: In the Taihe era, when Li Deyu held power, Shen was promoted to observation commissioner of Zhedong.
proposals.reason: 觀察使 is observation commissioner, not military commissioner (節度使).

proposals.before: He died and was posthumously made grand mentor with the posthumous title Wensu.
proposals.after: He died and was posthumously made grand commandant with the posthumous title Wensu.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant/Grand Marshal, not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wensu.
proposals.after: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous title Wensu.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant/Grand Marshal, not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: District people accused Xiang of rampant corruption and of marrying a commoner's daughter, Yan Yue.
proposals.after: District people accused Xiang of rampant corruption and of marrying the daughter of a commoner, Yan Yue.
proposals.reason: Chinese 娶民顏悅女 means he married Yan Yue's daughter; Yan Yue is the father, not the bride.

proposals.before: Shen had observation commissioner Wei Yin try Xiang; the case was clear and Xiang was sentenced to death.
proposals.after: Shen had observation-commission judicial reviewer Wei Yin try Xiang; the case was clear and Xiang was sentenced to death.
proposals.reason: 觀察判官 is a staff judicial reviewer, not the observation commissioner himself.

proposals.before: Li Guyuan urged Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong instead.
proposals.after: Li Guyan urged Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong instead.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李固言 is Li Guyan; 'Guyuan' misreads 固言.

proposals.before: Li Guyuan asked to use Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.
proposals.after: Li Guyan asked to use Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 李固言 is Li Guyan; 'Guyuan' misreads 固言.

proposals.before: At his son's wedding the emperor said, "Go home—I will send wine."
proposals.after: When his household was taking a bride, the emperor said, "Go home—I will send wine."
proposals.reason: Chinese 家嘗娶婦 does not specify a son; idiomatic invents 'son's wedding'.

proposals.before: Wenzong wanted the musician Yuchi Zhang as princely commandant; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi protested until Zhang was sent to Guangzhou as chief secretary.
proposals.after: Wenzong wanted the musician Yuchi Zhang as princely commandant; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi protested until Zhang was sent to Guang Prefecture as chief secretary.
proposals.reason: Chinese 光州 is Guang Prefecture, not Guangzhou (廣州).

proposals.before: Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi firmly protested, and Zhang was finally given long-term assignment as chief secretary of Guangzhou.
proposals.after: Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi firmly protested, and Zhang was finally given long-term assignment as chief secretary of Guang Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Chinese 光州 is Guang Prefecture (光州), not Guangzhou (廣州).

proposals.before: Thereafter Li Jue and Yang Sifu, blocked by Tan's influence, could not advance for the rest of Wenzong's reign.
proposals.after: Thereafter Li Jue and Yang Sifu, because of Tan's recommendation, could not advance for the rest of Wenzong's reign.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以覃之薦 means because of Tan's recommendation, not vague 'influence'.

proposals.before: Yizong completed the Chengan Kingdom shrine and received two jeweled thrones, each two zhang high, of heavy sandalwood lacquered and inlaid with gold, carved with dragons and phoenixes; canopy seats stood above sutra tables, with spirit figures at the corners and brocade hangings of surpassing splendor.
proposals.after: Yizong completed the Anguo shrine and bestowed two jeweled thrones, each two zhang high, of heavy sandalwood lacquered and inlaid with gold, carved with dragons and phoenixes; canopy seats stood above sutra tables, with spirit figures at the corners and brocade hangings of surpassing splendor.
proposals.reason: 成安國祠 means he completed (成) the Anguo (安國) shrine, not a place named Chengan Kingdom; 賜 is bestowal by the emperor, not receipt.

proposals.before: At the beginning Yizong completed the Chengan Kingdom shrine and was granted two jeweled thrones, each two zhang high, built of heavy sandalwood, lacquered, carved with dragons, phoenixes, and floral patterns, fastened with gold; a canopy seat was placed above, sutra tables set before them, auspicious birds and divine figures standing several feet tall at the four corners, with steps to ascend; the front was draped in embroidered bags and brocade skirts—rare and exquisite beyond compare.
proposals.after: Yizong completed the Anguo shrine and bestowed two jeweled thrones, each two zhang high, built of heavy sandalwood, lacquered, carved with dragons, phoenixes, and floral patterns, fastened with gold; a canopy seat was placed above, sutra tables set before them, auspicious birds and divine figures standing several feet tall at the four corners, with steps to ascend; the front was draped in embroidered bags and brocade skirts—rare and exquisite beyond compare.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 成 is the verb completed; 安國祠 is the Anguo shrine; 賜 means bestowed, not was granted.

proposals.before: First Chief Minister Wang Jin, preaching karma, persuaded Daizong to build an inner dharma hall with ceaseless chanting to ward off invaders, grand Ullambana rites, and ancestral images sent to temples—a spectacle that made rebels laugh.
proposals.after: At first, Chief Minister Wang Jin, preaching karma, persuaded Daizong to build an inner dharma hall with ceaseless chanting to ward off invaders, grand Ullambana rites, and ancestral images sent to temples—a spectacle that made rebel ministers laugh.
proposals.reason: 初 means at first/initially, not First as a rank before Chief Minister; 賊臣 is rebel ministers, not merely rebels.

proposals.before: He mourned in ignorance, begged a relic's protection, pledged his life without restraint, wept and prostrated himself—yet could not approach the ancestral temple or Heaven as he should.
proposals.after: He raised lament in a field of ignorance, begged shelter from a corpse of a hundred joints, pledged himself unto death without restraint, wept and prostrated himself—devotion that even serving the ancestral temple and the High God could not surpass.
proposals.reason: 雖事宗廟上帝，無以進焉 means his relic devotion went beyond even ancestral-temple and Shangdi worship, not that he failed to approach them as he should.

decisions.after: When a wedding was being celebrated in his household, the emperor said, "Go home; I will send wine."
decisions.reason: 家嘗娶婦 does not specify whose marriage it was. The revision removes the invented son while expressing the household event naturally in English.
卒授光州長史 posts him to Guang Prefecture (光州), not Guangzhou (廣州).

decisions.after: Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi firmly protested, and Zhang was finally appointed Chief Clerk of Guang Prefecture.
decisions.reason: 光州 is Guang Prefecture, not Guangzhou, and 長史 is the office Chief Clerk, not a 'long-term assignment'; the proposal fixed only the place name.

decisions.after: Afterward, because Zheng Tan had recommended him, Li Jue and Yang Sifu kept Rangyi from further promotion for the rest of Wenzong's reign.
decisions.reason: The omitted subject of 終帝世不得遷 is the biography's subject, Li Rangyi. Li Jue and Yang Sifu blocked him because he had been Zheng Tan's recommendation; the proposal wrongly made them the officials who failed to advance.

decisions.after: At first, Emperor Yizong completed the Anguo shrine and bestowed two jeweled seats, each two zhang high. They were made of agarwood and sandalwood, lacquered, carved with dragons, phoenixes, and flowers, and fitted with gold. Additional seats were placed above them and scripture tables before them; auspicious birds and divine figures several feet high stood at the four corners. Steps led up, while embroidered coverings and brocade valances draped the front. Their rarity and workmanship were unsurpassed.
decisions.reason: 成安國祠 refers to completing the Anguo shrine, and 賜 is the emperor's bestowal. The revision also renders 沈檀 as agarwood and sandalwood and turns the long inventory into readable English without dropping its details.

decisions.after: At first, Yizong completed the Anguo shrine and bestowed two jeweled seats measuring two zhang high. They were constructed of agarwood and sandalwood, coated with lacquer, carved with dragons, phoenixes, and flowers, and fastened with gold. Additional seats were set above them and scripture tables arranged before them. At the four corners stood auspicious birds and divine figures several feet high; steps provided access, and the front was covered with embroidered cloth and brocade valances. They were exceptionally rare, beautiful, and finely made.
decisions.reason: The revision preserves sentence-initial 始, reads 成安國祠 and 賜 correctly, renders 沈檀 as agarwood and sandalwood, and retains the physical inventory in grammatical literal English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 始，懿宗成安國祠，賜寶坐二

decisions.after: At first, Chief Minister Wang Jin supported Emperor Daizong with teachings about karma and merit. The palace then established an inner ritual sanctuary where Buddhist chants sounded day and night in hopes of warding off enemy armies. Grand Ullambana rites were held, images of the imperial ancestors were made and distributed among pagodas and temples, and rebel officials laughed at the spectacle.
decisions.reason: 初 is temporal, 緣業 refers to teachings of karma and merit, and 賊臣 means rebel officials. The revision restores the source's sequence and removes the proposal's compressed list construction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初，宰相王縉…為賊臣嘻笑

decisions.after: He raised a lament before an insensible thing and begged protection from the disjointed remains of a corpse. Pledging himself to it unto death without thought of restraint, he wept and prostrated himself with a devotion that even worship of the ancestral temple and the Lord on High could not surpass.
decisions.reason: 雖事宗廟上帝，無以進焉 says that his devotion to the Buddha's bodily relic surpassed even service to the ancestral temple and the Lord on High. The revision preserves the historian's contempt in 無知 and 百解之胔 without the opaque phrase 'corpse of a hundred joints.'

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雖事宗廟上帝，無以進焉
